name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,467

clue.text: Supply account of beers I'd drunk around clubs

indicators.note: drink has gone to these words' heads, so their letters stagger into a new order
the jumbled letters wrap themselves round the next piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Someone owning up to having knocked back beers while touring nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled DESRIBE wraps round C to give DESCRIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: To describe something is to give an account of it, to supply a verbal picture of what happened.

clue.text: Damage reputation of French musical

blocks.note: de is French for of
Fame is a musical about a New York performing arts school

explanation.surface: Accusing a French musical of harming someone's good name.
explanation.definitionFit: To defame is to harm someone's good name by making false statements about them.

clue.text: Short of muscle and short of money having spent time by US city

indicators.note: what has been spent is gone, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: skint is British slang for broke
T is the abbreviation for time
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A weedy, penniless visitor who has burned through cash and time in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Skint is everyday British slang for having no money; drop its T and add NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny means very thin, lacking flesh or bulk on the body.

clue.text: Speedy driver, one in luxury car

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other

blocks.note: RR stands for Rolls-Royce
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A fast motorist sitting in a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.definitionFit: A racer is someone who competes in races, here at the wheel, so a driver who goes fast.

clue.text: After being cast, replace broody actor

indicators.note: casting can mean throwing about, so the letters are flung into a new pattern

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A film studio swapping out a moody star once the roles have been assigned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' plays on a film cast, which fits the actor perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bradley Cooper is an American film star known for The Hangover and A Star Is Born.

clue.text: Piece of wood male found in river

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the Tiber is the river through Rome
M is the standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A log turned up floating in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber is wood prepared for building, and a single beam or plank can be called a timber.

clue.text: One that's unable to be out?

definitions.text: One that's unable to be out?

blocks.clueFragment: One that's unable to be out?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone stuck at home, unable to go out
setter's reading: out means unconscious, out cold, so this is someone who cannot fall asleep

explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' suggests leaving the house, but being out also means being asleep or knocked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with insomnia lies awake at night, unable to drop off into unconsciousness.

clue.text: Diverting prank but devoid of substance

indicators.note: to divert is to send off course, so the letters are turned in a new direction

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A review of a practical joke that was amusing yet empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diverting' reads as entertaining, describing the prank, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Bankrupt describes something wholly lacking in a quality, as in morally bankrupt, empty of worth.

clue.text: Auditor's studied skill about the French in a crisis situation

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is taken as heard rather than spelt
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: the past tense read is said like the colour
art is skill or craft
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An accountant's examined skills during an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant but here simply means a listener; studied is the past tense, said like the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Red alert is the highest state of readiness, declared when danger is imminent.

clue.text: Become excited by daily end to broadcast - part of a presentation?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: to flip is to lose control or get very worked up
a daily is a cleaning lady, also called a char or charwoman
the final letter of broadcast

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled at the closing moments of a radio or TV show, with a nod to giving a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper but is the British cleaner, a char, who comes in every day.
explanation.definitionFit: A flip chart is a large pad of paper on a stand, a common visual aid when speakers give talks.

clue.text: Gangsters without good right vie furiously about end of heists - typical of them?

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that letter is dropped
acting furiously means wildly, throwing the letters into disorder
the end of a word is its last letter, the only one kept
about means going round, so the jumbled letters enclose the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written
the final letter of heists

explanation.surface: Crooks losing a member, competing angrily over the proceeds of robberies.
explanation.walkthrough: Gangsters minus a G, plus R and VIE, is jumbled round S. The definition leans on the surface: law-breaking is what gangsters do.
explanation.definitionFit: Transgressive means breaking rules or laws, characteristic behaviour of the criminals in the clue.

clue.text: Church body straightaway after vacation to show approval

indicators.note: vacating a word empties out its interior, leaving only its outer letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of straightaway
a nod of the head signals agreement

explanation.surface: A church committee giving its blessing immediately after the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vacation' looks like a holiday but means emptying the word straightaway of its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of clergy and church members that governs a church or diocese.

clue.text: It's mixed among relation's sandwiches

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling between slices, so the letters lie inside these words

blocks.note: letters running across the two words, hidden between the a and the ation's

explanation.surface: A packed lunch of assorted fillings handed round among family members.
explanation.definitionFit: A mongrel is a dog of mixed breed, so 'it's mixed' describes one cryptically.

clue.text: Revolutionary car retaining part of wheel, one that's top in fleet?

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the result is read backwards
to retain is to hold on to, so the car keeps the other piece inside it

blocks.note: Lada is a Russian make of car
the rim is a wheel's outer edge

explanation.surface: A Soviet-era car with a wheel part still attached, and a nautical title tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: LA(RIM)DA is built first, then the whole thing is read backwards. 'Revolutionary' suggests Russia, the Lada's homeland, which is part of the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is the highest-ranking naval officer, commanding a fleet of warships.

clue.text: Large spidery petal's not alien possibly in an orchid

indicators.note: 'not' tells you to leave the following item out of the letters
possibly signals one of several possible arrangements of the letters

blocks.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
ET is the film's extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: A botanist describing a flower with long, thin petals that looks strangely otherworldly.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E and T from L+SPIDERY+PETALS, then rearrange the twelve letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady's slipper is a wild orchid named for its pouch-shaped lip, which resembles a little shoe.

clue.text: A criminal besetting men within hour is loathsome

indicators.note: to beset is to surround on all sides, so this piece wraps round the rest
within puts one item inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
bent is slang for corrupt or crooked
HR is the abbreviation for hour
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A crook surrounding soldiers inside an hour is a horrible thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Two nested containers: men sit within hour, and criminal besets the result. Other ranks is the crossword stock meaning of men; bent is British slang for crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrent means inspiring disgust and hatred, the same as loathsome.

clue.text: Rating given to hotel in resort of Dubai - or Dubai's neighbour

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort the following letters again
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: an AB, able-bodied seaman, is a naval rating
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A star rating awarded to a hotel in a Dubai holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday destination, which suits the surface, but it splits as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is the emirate and capital city bordering Dubai in the United Arab Emirates.

clue.text: Financial district with pull, we hear, in local US administration

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word is matched by its sound

blocks.note: the City is London's financial centre
to haul is to pull

explanation.surface: Wall Street influence over municipal government.
explanation.definitionFit: City hall is the American name for a municipal government and its headquarters.

clue.text: Book by absolutely correct and sure type, a classic thriller

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
an emphatic way of saying exactly right
a dependable person is called a rock

explanation.surface: A literary reference to a novel by a principled, confident author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like part of the definition but supplies only B. Brighton Rock is also a seaside sweet, a stick of hard candy sold at Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton Rock is Graham Greene's 1938 crime novel about the gangster Pinkie Brown, a celebrated thriller.

clue.text: Show noted tennis player getting up infused with energy

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards
infused means steeped through, so the next piece is put inside

blocks.note: Rod Laver, the Australian who won two calendar Grand Slams
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A famous tennis star rising, full of energy, for an exhibition match.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something is to show it, bringing it into view.

clue.text: Outsiders in some level at college to cancel debt

indicators.note: the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters, taken from each of the next two words

blocks.note: the first and last letters of some
the first and last letters of level
a student in residence at university is up

explanation.surface: A student at some stage of college trying to clear what they owe.
explanation.walkthrough: Up is the British idiom for being in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell up is to sell one's home or business entirely, often to pay off what is owed.

clue.text: Duke meets party I arranged for short excursion

indicators.note: things arranged are put in a fresh order, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An aristocrat joins a group on an outing someone has organised.
explanation.definitionFit: A day trip is a journey somewhere and back within a single day, a brief outing.

clue.text: Very powerful backing for soul singer

blocks.note: first meaning: highest in authority
second meaning: a member of the Motown group that backed Diana Ross

explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like a reversal signal, but here it is a backing singer: the Supremes were billed as Diana Ross and the Supremes.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means having the greatest power, and one of the Supremes sang behind the soul star Diana Ross.

clue.text: Two Greek characters in religious depiction

blocks.note: pi is the sixteenth Greek letter
eta is the seventh Greek letter

explanation.surface: Greek lettering on an icon in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies both letters, PI then ETA.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of the Virgin Mary cradling the dead Christ.

clue.text: A jar right off for semiprecious stone

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, so a letter drops out of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
to jar is to grate, as a harsh noise grates on the ears
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A pot with its correct lid missing being swapped for a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jar' looks like a container noun but is the verb, grate; take out its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded variety of chalcedony quartz, valued as an ornamental gemstone of modest worth.

clue.text: Commend oil company removing leaders - and cause a lot of trouble

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters, and these are taken away

blocks.note: to commend is to speak well of
Shell is the multinational oil firm

explanation.surface: A protest group praising an oil firm while ousting its bosses and stirring things up.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words lose their first letters, giving RAISE and HELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise hell is an idiom for creating a noisy disturbance or making angry complaints.

clue.text: Fashionable rental properties in coastal features

blocks.note: what is in is in fashion
a let is a property rented out

explanation.surface: Trendy holiday lets on the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: Inlets are narrow arms of sea reaching into the land, typical of a shoreline.

clue.text: Flag poem reviewed as a huge failure

indicators.note: viewed again in a new way, so the letters are set out differently

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Critics panning a patriotic poem about a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A flop is a failure, and the prefix mega- intensifies it into a spectacular one.
